resources.string: Use the default delay, or choose a shorter or longer delay for this app. Global changes wait for the default delay first. This app waits longer only if its own delay is longer; shorter app delays cannot start a global change early. An app-only change uses this app’s own delay. Temporary global changes have one shared end time, so this app may get less time or none. Increasing a delay takes effect immediately. Reducing it waits for the difference: changing 6 hours to 4 hours waits 2 hours. Returning to a shorter default delay follows the same rule.
Global changes use the default delay. This app stays protected until its longer wait ends. App-only changes use this app’s delay.

This global change waits for the default delay. Apps with longer delays stay protected until their own wait ends. Shorter app delays cannot start a global change early. A temporary global pause has one shared end time.
Apps with longer delays stay protected. Tap the main switch to see their end times.
Protection stays off until you enable it.
DomainGuard will stay on.\n\nCancel the %1$s pause scheduled to start at %2$s.
Your existing rules will apply again immediately.\n\nThe pause was due to end at %1$s.
The pause changed. Please review its current state.
The wait starts when you tap %1$s. Your current rules stay active during the wait.
The wait starts when you tap Pause. DomainGuard keeps protecting you during the wait. Your %1$s pause starts afterward.
This change takes effect when you confirm.

DomainGuard pause: countdown and Cancel while pending; countdown and Resume while paused. Both actions ask for confirmation. The main switch gently fades while a global change is pending or active; tap it to see which apps remain protected and their end times.
